notes:
**Get remote help, right from VP Studio.** Help ▸ Get remote help… asks TNR Developments for a hand — no TeamViewer, no RemotePC, nothing to install. You see a six-digit number to read out if you are on the phone; when someone at TNR picks the request up you get an Allow / Not now prompt, and nothing happens until you click Allow. While they help, a dark bar stays across the top of your screen saying who is connected and for how long, with Chat, End, and a ▾ that shrinks the bar to a small tab if it covers something. You keep your own mouse and keyboard the whole time; their pointer shows with their name, and they can draw a circle or an arrow on your screen to point something out (the marks vanish when the session ends). End, or closing the PC, stops everything at once.

**What remote help can and cannot do.** They can see this screen, use the mouse and keyboard, message you in the chat window (which opens by itself on their first message), and send or fetch files — anything they send you lands in Desktop ▸ From TNR Developments, and a file never overwrites one of yours. They cannot connect on their own, act on Windows permission prompts, unlock the PC, or delete your files. Nothing is installed and nothing stays behind. The licence agreement (section 5) and tnrdevelopments.com/privacy say exactly what is kept: the session record, file names and the chat — never the screen itself.

**Your licence follows the portal.** Each time VP Studio starts it checks whether TNR has issued a newer key for this PC and applies it on its own — a temporary key made permanent, or a feature added or removed, no longer needs the key typed in again.

**VP-IL: the head bridge ruler.** On a machine whose bridge carries TNR's mm ruler (0 at the belt centre, + up), the placement popup and the Studio canvas now say exactly where to set each head — "set Head 1 to +63.5 mm" — instead of an inch measurement, draw the belt-centre line, and let Head 2 sit above Head 1 when the design wants it. A feeder that cannot centre a piece gets a per-job offset, and a check print can be turned into a per-head correction in Settings ▸ Machine. Machines without the ruler are unchanged.

**Small things.** The installer's licensing page no longer names a real dealer in its example.
